title: Baked Stuffed Shells
subtitle: Italian-American conchiglioni filled with ricotta and baked in tomato
excerpt: Large pasta shells are filled with a ricotta and mozzarella mixture, nestled into a tomato sauce, and baked under a bubbling cheese topping. A crowd-pleasing baked pasta that works well made ahead.
sourceNotes: Italian-American baked stuffed shells with ricotta filling, a classic of the New York Italian-American table.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled but unbaked. Cover tightly. Bake from frozen at 200C for 55 minutes, covered, then uncover for 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the bake time if cold from the fridge.

content.text: Large conchiglioni shells need slightly less cooking before filling, as they finish in the oven. Don't cram the shells; they need a little space to sit upright in the sauce. Rest the dish before serving so the filling firms up slightly.

items.prepNote: half grated, half torn into pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Cook the shells in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and spread on a tray to cool.
Make the sauce. Warm the olive oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the passata, season, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, grated mozzarella, half the parmesan, the egg, nutmeg, and most of the basil in a bowl. Season well.
Spread two thirds of the tomato sauce over the base of the roasting tin.
Fill each shell with a heaped spoonful of the ricotta mixture. Tuck the filled shells opening-side up into the sauce.
Spoon the remaining tomato sauce over the top. Scatter the torn mozzarella and remaining parmesan over everything.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake for a further 10 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with remaining basil.

items.fix: Cook 2 full minutes less than the packet time. They finish in the oven.

items.symptom: The filling is watery after baking.
items.fix: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for 30 minutes before mixing. Pat dry if needed.

items.symptom: The top is burnt before the centre is hot.
items.cause: The oven runs hot, or the tin was uncovered too early.
items.fix: Keep the foil on for the full first 25 minutes and lower the shelf by one position.
